detailed_findings.finding: The conversion of R_{a,b,r}(q) from the q-Pochhammer quotient to the finite product over i = a+1,...,b is correct.
The factorwise computation of (1 - q^{-(r+i)})/(1 - q^{-i}) gives q^{-r}(1 - q^{r+i})/(1 - q^i), yielding the stated self-reciprocity identity after multiplication.
The argument excluding coefficients d_j with j > D by uncancellable negative powers is sound, and the final reindexing establishes palindromicity of coefficients.

reason: The proof is correct and complete. It handles the empty-product case a = b separately, then for a < b rewrites the q-Pochhammer quotient as the stated finite product, checks factor-by-factor that substitution q -> q^(-1) contributes exactly a factor q^(-r) per term, and therefore derives q^D R_{a,b,r}(q^(-1)) = R_{a,b,r}(q) with D = r(b-a). Under the additional assumption R_{a,b,r}(q) in Z[q], it expands R as a polynomial, uses the self-reciprocity identity to rule out terms of degree > D by the appearance of uncancellable negative powers, pads coefficients to length D, and compares coefficients to obtain c_j = c_{D-j}. This matches the lemma sketch exactly and uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
